title: KnowledgeDeletionAcknowledged
description:
Payload of `knowledge.deletion.acknowledged.v1`: Knowledge tells a producer that one of its
deletion facts was applied or refused.

The enclosing event envelope is produced by `ratatoskr-knowledge`. Its `event_id` is the
outbox id, `aggregate_id` equals `subject`, `correlation_id` is copied from
the acknowledged envelope, `causation_id` is `event:<acknowledged_event_id>` and `tenant_id`
equals `owner`.

The acknowledgement names no content: only ids, the owner and a subject reference. A
producer matches it to the outbox row whose `event_id` equals
`acknowledged_event_id` and whose tenant equals
`owner`, and ignores one that matches no row. A duplicate acknowledgement
changes nothing.

`validate()` runs on every deserialization, so a payload that violates the
outcome rule never reaches a consumer.

acknowledged_at.description: Instant Knowledge decided the outcome, according to the Knowledge clock.

acknowledged_event_id.description: The `event_id` of the deletion fact this acknowledgement answers.

family.description: Which deletion fact family was answered.

outcome.description: Whether the deletion was applied or refused.

owner.description: The owner of the deleted data.

refusal.description: Why the deletion was refused. Present exactly when `outcome` is `refused`.

subject.description: The subject the deletion fact named, as an opaque reference.

EntityRef.title: EntityRef
EntityRef.description: A namespaced, polymorphic wire reference, serialized as `<kind>:<local_id>`. The kind vocabulary is open: an unrecognised kind is preserved verbatim. The local identity is opaque and need not be a UUID; when it is one it must be the canonical lowercase hyphenated spelling, so one identity has one reference. Equality is octet equality of `<kind>:<local_id>`: the kind is lowercase by grammar, and the local part is case-sensitive and never case-folded, because provider identities are case-significant. This rule is narrower than the `pattern` below, which cannot express it.

EventId.title: EventId
EventId.description: Identity of one event occurrence, and the at-least-once deduplication key. Bare canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID; not namespaced.

TenantRef.title: TenantRef
TenantRef.description: The owner of the data a record concerns, wire form `user:<uuid>`. The kind set is closed: a consumer that cannot understand the owner kind must reject the record rather than process it.

WireTimestamp.title: WireTimestamp
WireTimestamp.description: An instant on the wire: RFC 3339 in UTC with the literal `Z` designator. Exactly one spelling is accepted per instant — an input that does not re-render to itself is rejected. The field holding it declares the clock authority.
